summary: Preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute a 711KB obfuscated sibling bundle unrelated to the advertised CLI
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with hex-named identifiers and string-lookup indirection; when invoked it checks for a local bun binary and, if absent, downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts and chmods it, then execFileSync's the downloaded bun against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with a shuffled numeric/string constant array (n7gIxM) and mangled variable names — no source, no documentation, no relation to the advertised ~6KB permissions-YAML-uploader CLI. Fetching an alternate language runtime at install time solely to execute a large obfuscated sibling payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the executed bytes are not the aggressive-but-legitimate case of installing a runtime to run the package's own transparent shipped code, and Node-based inspection tooling will not analyze the Bun-executed payload. The auto-execute-on-default-install gate is satisfied via the preinstall lifecycle hook, and the payload's purpose is opaque and mismatched to the package's stated function.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
